gaps.issue: The claim that the second source's multiplier-ideal condition is "the same condition as Cao's after writing λ'=λ(1+δ)" is inaccurate. The second source defines I(φ) using |f|²exp(-φ), whereas Cao uses |f|²exp(-2φ); moreover, the second source quantifies over all real λ'>λ>0, while Cao quantifies over m∈N and δ>0. Admissibility is still obtainable, but the proof must explicitly use I_Cao(aφ)=I_second(2aφ) and apply the second source's inclusion with λ=2m and λ'=2m(1+δ).

repair_hints: [pi_c446657f9d449fbe5fdd0abd] Replace the asserted equality of definitions by the precise one-way comparison: because I_Cao(aφ)=I_second(2aφ), the second source's condition at λ=2m and λ'=2m(1+δ) gives I_Cao(m(1+δ)φ_j)⊆I_Cao(mφ) for every m∈N and δ>0. Thus the gentle approximation is admissible for Cao's Definition 3, without claiming that the two definitions are identical.
